The lighthouse stands alone on its rocky headland, a pale column of weathered stone gone soft and violet in the failing light. The sky behind it burns orange at the horizon, fading upward through rose and bruised purple into the first deep blue of night. Below, the sea heaves slowly, its surface catching the last copper glints of the vanished sun while the waves fold against the rocks in long, white-lipped sighs.

Then the lamp wakes. A warm gold glow gathers in the lantern room, and the great beam begins its patient circle, sweeping out over the water in a slow, sure arc. Gulls wheel homeward, dark scraps against the dimming clouds. The air smells of salt and cold stone, and the wind carries the faint clang of a distant buoy. One by one the stars appear, small and unhurried, as the lighthouse takes up its nightly vigil, steady and silent, keeping faith with every ship still out in the dark.
